If any of the checked exceptions (InstantiationException, NoSuchMethodException, InvocationTargetException, IllegalAccessException) are thrown during the instantiation, the method catches these exceptions, logs an error message, and then throws a RuntimeException with a custom message. The use of a RuntimeException here suggests that the programmer considers the inability to instantiate the timer as an exceptional and unrecoverable condition within this method. However, the fact that the method logs an error before throwing the RuntimeException implies that the programmer expects the caller to be aware of this potential failure and possibly handle it, even though it is not mandatory.
